summary: Client cache of mod.io mod info, written by ls::ugc::ModInfoCachedRequestSystem::GatherRequests: HashMap<ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID, net::PublishModInfo> plus a POD array at +0x40 (by analogy with CacheModDependenciesSingleton: pending ModItemInfoIDs). The map is written out member by member because its key is a struct. Live: idle, all zero.

fields.name: ModId
fields.evidence: ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID +0: macOS HashTable<ModItemInfoID>::Ensure (bg3_macos_x64+0x260BA40) hashes and compares this qword first; Windows default (bg3.exe+0x3BE8230) 0. Named by analogy with ModItemDependenciesInfoID's 64-bit item id.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: Value of an optional 64-bit member: Ensure compares it (and mixes it into the hash) only when the flag at +0x10 is set on both sides; Windows default 0 (8-byte store).

fields.name: field_8HasValue
fields.evidence: The flag of the optional at +8 (Ensure: 'if flag == 0, value hashed as 0'; compared as bool); Windows default 0 (8-byte zero store at +0x10).

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: Compared as one byte by Ensure; Windows default byte 0 at +0x18.

fields.name: field_1C
fields.evidence: Compared and hashed as a 4-byte int by Ensure; Windows default 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) at +0x1C.

fields.name: HashKeys
fields.evidence: Bucket table of ls::HashMap<ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID, ls::ugc::ModItemInfoResponse> (macOS EnsureNode/Remove of that type); creator bg3.exe+0x3BEA620 zeroes 0x50; destructor bg3.exe+0x3B7A240 -> bg3.exe+0x3B7CF00 destroys the values and the plain-key set (bg3.exe+0x582AD0). Written member by member because the key is a struct.

fields.name: NextIds
fields.evidence: Hash chain array of the ls::HashTable.

fields.name: Keys
fields.evidence: Key array, 0x20-byte ModItemInfoID elements (Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE9490 indexes keys with stride 0x20; macOS Ensure stride 0x20).

fields.name: Values
fields.evidence: Value storage, one ls::ugc::ModItemInfoResponse per key, 0x150-byte stride on Windows: bg3.exe+0x3B7CF00 runs bg3.exe+0x38B5D20 (the net::PublishModInfo destructor, also used for ModList entries) on value+8 for every key; bg3.exe+0x3BE9490 copies a response as qword +0, PublishModInfo +8 (0x140 bytes, bg3.exe+0x3BDF700) and the 4 bytes at +0x148. Spelled out as raw parts (a struct key forbids the HashMap form).

fields.name: RecentIds
fields.evidence: Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE9490: each cached id is found/moved (bg3.exe+0x3BEA400/+0x3BEA4B0) or appended (bg3.exe+0x3BEA240) in the 0x20-byte-stride array at +0x40 (count +0x4C); then 'while (count > 30)' the last entry is popped and its response removed from the map - an LRU list capping the cache at 30 mod infos. Destructor frees it as a plain array (bg3.exe+0x5BD630).

open_questions: Meaning of ModItemInfoID's optional qword at +8, the byte at +0x18 and the int at +0x1C (default -1).
The 0x140-byte net::PublishModInfo and the response's +0 qword / +0x148 int are kept inside the raw value storage.
second_pass: Settled on Windows: bg3.exe+0x3BE9490 shows 0x20-byte keys, 0x150-byte ModItemInfoResponse values (PublishModInfo at +8) and the +0x40 LRU array capped at 30; the key's members come from the macOS hash/compare (bg3_macos_x64+0x260BA40) and match the Windows defaults in bg3.exe+0x3BE8230.
